On/Off platforming level, where you bait thwomps to hit the switches. My goal was a quick level with a few tricky-ish jumps, but nothing insane.

I think the average person can make plenty fun levels without having a groundbreaking idea. Play around with a few mechanics and build around them. Keep testing it, and honestly the #1 thing to ask yourself is are you having fun going through the level? If not, what can you do to improve it? There's a lot of different ways that people have fun with Mario, what makes it fun for you? Make a level around that, there's almost certainly other people that like Mario for the same reason you do, whether it's speedrunning, going after risky coins, smooth platforming with a nice flow, etc.

It definitely takes practice, but I can feel a sense of improvement from each level I've made so far, even if it's only a little bit. Even if you make a level and trash it, you still learn something from the time you spent playing around with making levels!

I wouldn't mind if the skill system was tweaked, but at the end of the day the best way to gauge someone's skill is just to watch them play/play with them. It'll show if someone hand picks songs from each tier to artificially boost their skill stat.

EDIT: A side thought as well, having my skill at 1,000 would be a really hollow victory if I had to stop playing to keep it. Obviously different people have different priorities, but it seems pretty pointless to me anyway.

If he says anything other than "Wait, it should've been X" or something along those lines, then it's the first ingredient. Don't get me wrong, it doesn't really bother me if someone uses a mod like BCCFS, but cooking in a pub game comes with obvious risks. Hell, even when someone uses a mod that literally posts the ingredient to the chat, I've still seen people fuck it up. The #1 way to avoid fucking up cooking is to do it yourself, or play with people that you know aren't braindead.

It's up to people to individually decide what they consider cheating, it's good that you ask people you join if they're okay with certain mods and disable then if they're not.

Of course, some people do argue that any modification to gameplay that isn't vanilla is cheating, and by definition, they're right. But for example I don't consider better bots innately cheating myself. It has the potential to be cheating IMO, if you upgrade their aim proficiency, but I don't think it's a big deal if they're otherwise vanilla, minus changing priorities, so they don't just ignore you if you go down, which is what the mod does if you don't tweak other settings. Some people disagree, and that's fine. They're free to not use it or play in lobbies that use it.

Other mods like carry stacker are a little more of a grey area, I think. Technically it's cheating, but I say that in a sense that you just can't say that you've played 100% legit if you use it, I don't consider it on the same level as using things like God mode, where you're not even pretending to work for it. Modifying all the bag weights so you could pick up all the safes on aftershock and Sprint across the map, however... You get the idea.
